entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Thanks for joining. To start, could you tell me a little about yourself?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: Thank you for having me. I have spent the last few years working across product teams, mostly on customer-facing tools, and I enjoy the part of the work where a vague problem turns into something people can actually use.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Great. What drew you to this role in particular?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: The role combines two things I care about: working closely with users and having enough ownership to see a piece of work through from the first conversation to the release.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Could you walk me through a recent project you are proud of?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: Sure. The most recent one was a redesign of an onboarding flow. Completion had dropped, so I started by watching session recordings and talking to five customers before changing anything.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: How did you decide what to prioritise when the deadline moved?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I listed what was blocking people, ranked the items by how many users each one affected, and agreed the top three with the team. Everything else went into a later milestone.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Okay.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: Yes.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: What would you do differently if you ran that project again?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I would involve support earlier. They already knew about two of the issues we only discovered in testing, and that would have saved about a week.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: How do you usually handle disagreement within a team?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I try to separate the decision from the people. I write down the options, what each one costs, and what we would need to see to change our minds, then we pick one and review it after a fixed period.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Can you give me a concrete example of that?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: On one project we disagreed about whether to rebuild a component or patch it. We agreed to patch it, set a date to revisit, and when the date came the data made the rebuild an easy call.

entries.text: The role combines two things I care about: working closely with users and having enough ownership to see a piece of work through from the first conversation to the release.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Could you walk me through a recent project you are proud of?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: Sure. The most recent one was a redesign of an onboarding flow. Completion had dropped, so I started by watching session recordings and talking to five customers before changing anything.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I listed what was blocking people, ranked the items by how many users each one affected, and agreed the top three with the team. Everything else went into a later milestone.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: How did you decide what to prioritise when the deadline moved?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: Yes.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: Okay.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I would involve support earlier. They already knew about two of the issues we only discovered in testing, and that would have saved about a week.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: What would you do differently if you ran that project again?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: I try to separate the decision from the people. I write down the options, what each one costs, and what we would need to see to change our minds, then we pick one and review it after a fixed period.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: On one project we disagreed about whether to rebuild a component or patch it. We agreed to patch it, set a date to revisit, and when the date came the data made the rebuild an easy call.

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWER
entries.text: How do you usually handle disagreement within a team?

entries.speaker: INTERVIEWEE
entries.text: We tracked completion rate and time to first action. Completion went up within the first two weeks and stayed there, and support tickets on that flow dropped.
